notes:
Overview: Velox Outbound Labs is a mid-market SaaS company building an outbound SDR/chat agent layer that executes multi-step sales actions (email drafts, CRM updates, meeting scheduling).

What they told us: "Need sub-300ms perceived latency for streaming UI, and tool calls (CRM/email/calendar) must complete reliably within ~1s to feel real-time to users."

Primary interest: start on Redwood Hosted API for speed of integration + streaming & function/tool calling. If POC meets latency SLOs, move to Dedicated reserved pool for predictable throughput and lower unit cost.

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria:
- Workload: outbound chat agents (agent orchestration + streaming responses) with tool calling to Salesforce, Gmail, Google Calendar.
- Latency SLO target: p95 <= 250-300ms for token streaming in our UI (end-to-end experience) under expected load.
- Throughput: support ~30 concurrent conversational agents per region initially; scale plan up to 300 agents (burst to 600) over 6 months.
- Reliability: fallbacks for model failures; prefer automatic routing to smaller/cheaper variants if capacity constrained.
- Model preferences: mixture of high-quality generative model for response + smaller reranker/embedding models for context retrieval. Open models OK if performance pixel-perfect; also evaluating Redwood-verified models.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market price pressure — looking for clear unit cost breakdown (tokens + reserved capacity options).
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, US data residency for PII, encryption-at-rest + in-transit.

POC plan (agreed): 2-week functional POC + 1-week performance window.
- Week 1: integrate Hosted API into prototype agent UI + connect to SFDC sandbox (restricted dataset). Smoke tests: streaming, basic tool calls.
- Week 2: run synthetic traffic to measure p95/p99 tail latencies; instrument token-level cost and latency. Mid-POC checkpoint with Diego and product lead.
- Performance window (3 days): 24/7 stress runs with real-ish scripts, collect traces for Redwood Console.
- Success criteria: p95 streaming <= 300ms, tool call success >= 99.5%, token cost within target band agreed during pricing call.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-01-09: inbound trial signup, basic discovery form answered.
- 2026-01-15: discovery call (owner Maya) — product overview, initial constraints captured.
- 2026-02-01: deep-dive with infra + product (SE Diego) — discussed streaming + function calling, SFDC integration.
- 2026-02-12: security questionnaire sent (drive://velox/security-questions).
- 2026-03-02: POC kickoff (ff_20260302_poc_kickoff).
- 2026-03-08: mid-POC sync — initial perf looks good on small scale, heavy tail spikes observed at noon sim.
- 2026-03-12: pricing call scheduled to align on reserved capacity options & estimated ARR.

Stated risks / notes from calls:
- "If we can't hit sub-300ms in the hosted environment we will need to move fast to Dedicated; procurement cycles are 6-8 weeks for dedicated contracts."
- Concern about token-level cost surprises during scale — wants transparent billing + tooling to show cost per-agent.
- Needs a canary/rollback strategy for model updates; product team asked about Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization and batching.

Open items / actions for Redwood team:
- Provide a tailored POC template and perf-run checklist (Diego to share by 2026-03-14).
- Provide sample streaming p95/p99 dashboards and token-cost breakdown for a comparable mid-market customer.
- Confirm compatibility with SFDC sandbox API rate limits and best practices for bulk updates.
- Prepare Dedicated sizing/pricing options assuming 300-600 agent peak load.

Customer quote highlights: "We need the agent to feel instantaneous — streaming latency and toolcall turnaround are make-or-break. If Hosted can hit the numbers, we prefer it for speed; otherwise Dedicated is an OK tradeoff for predictability."

Next meeting: pricing + reserved capacity options (internal pricing deck link: drive://velox/rdx-pricing-draft).
